decisions.reason: A quantified customer saving claim and the product’s close fit with the firm’s modular core business make its value largely validated, so keeping it is the more rational option.
As a flagship modular line aligned with the firm’s stated strategic direction, C still carries high strategic option value and would be abandoned only if clear negative evidence emerged.
D remains close to the core range and cheap enough to keep as an option, but with less visible proof of market traction than A or C it faces a meaningfully higher risk of withdrawal.

Although the earlier withdrawal of B shows discipline in this category, E is a newly launched multi-model shredder line in a familiar market space, so management would usually give it more time before judging it.
F is a new line that builds on the established offer and fits the firm’s growth and innovation path, so uncertainty is still worth carrying for another year.
